description: A connected subscriber bound at one site falls behind live delivery on a bounded log: one of its OWN events is appended and aged out before it can be woken for it, while the rest of the retained tail sits in a sibling site it cannot read. The server must mark the discontinuity with a buffer_exceeded gap whose from_id is the last id it actually DELIVERED to that subscriber (not the highest id its stream merely considered and suppressed) and whose to_id is the first retained id that subscriber may READ — so the marker names no id outside its visible set at either end, and delivery then resumes at to_id with no further silent loss.

phase_vocabulary.before_connect: recorded before the subscriber connects; resolved as its backlog
phase_vocabulary.live_before_loss: recorded through the ordinary write path while the subscriber is connected and draining. It is placed in the sibling site, so the subscriber CONSIDERS it and is not sent it — which is what moves its stream watermark off its last-delivered id, and therefore what makes from_id and the watermark two different values.
phase_vocabulary.undrained: recorded while the subscriber is parked mid-write and cannot drain — the burst it loses the race to. Retention 4 means 01J8Z3K4N5P6Q7R8S9T0V1W213, the subscriber's OWN event, is appended and aged out inside this burst: a genuinely lost eligible event, which is what the gap has to cover.
phase_vocabulary.live: recorded through the ordinary write path after the burst, in the subscriber's own site — the first id it may read above the discontinuity, and therefore where its delivery resumes.
